description: Works out a restaurant's break-even sales from the owner's own figures for one typical month, as the free break-even calculator on restaurantdoctorai.com does: the sales a month needs to pay every bill, also as a week, a day open and guests a day, how far the month's sales were above or short of it, what was left over after every bill, and what a point of cost moves it by. Hourly pay can rise with sales or stay fixed; when the owner isn't sure, it's worked out both ways as a range. Takes net sales, food and drink purchases, hourly pay, other costs that rise with sales and the bills that stay the same, plus an optional average spend, days open, stock counts and goal, in any currency; a figure that isn't sent is never counted as 0. Returns the calculator's result, how it was worked out, and a link that opens the calculator with the same figures filled in. The figures aren't stored; only an anonymous daily count of calculator runs is kept.

averageSpend.description: Optional: average spend per guest, the POS average check or net sales ÷ guests or orders. Turns sales into guests.

closingStock.description: Optional: stock at cost at the end of the month. Used only with openingStock.

daysPerWeek.description: Optional: days open a week, a whole number from 1 to 7. Turns the month into sales a day open (and guests a day, with averageSpend); left out, the day figures are left out.

fixedBills.description: A month of the bills that stay the same however busy it is: rent and utilities, salaries with their payroll taxes and benefits, insurance, software, marketing, loan and lease payments in full, and the owner's own pay if it isn't on payroll (left out, break-even assumes they work for free). No depreciation. Yearly bills ÷ 12. Required.

goal.description: Optional: what the owner would like left over each month after every bill, before income tax. Adds the sales a month that would take.

hourly.description: Whether hourly staff time goes up and down with sales: yes if shifts are added and cut as it gets busy or quiet; no if about the same team works every shift, so hourly pay is a bill that stays the same; unsure (the default) works it out both ways, as a range.

hourlyPay.description: That month's hourly wages from payroll, plus the employer's payroll taxes and benefits on them; no tips. Paid every two weeks: one pay run × 26 ÷ 12. Required: 0 with no hourly staff.

openingStock.description: Optional: stock at cost at the start of the month. Used only with closingStock: food and drink then becomes what was used, opening + purchases - closing. Skip both if stock stayed about the same.

otherVariable.description: That month's other costs that rise with every sale: card fees, delivery app commissions (app sales minus payouts), to-go packaging, any percentage rent, royalties or ad fund fees. Nothing already in the food and drink invoices. Required: 0 if none.

purchases.description: That month's food and drink supplier invoices, added up by delivery date. Required.

sales.description: Net sales for one typical month, in the owner's own currency like every figure here: the POS sales summary, before tax and tips, delivery app orders at menu price. Not a holiday rush or a one-off: every figure is for that same month. Required, and more than 0.

name: restaurantdoctor_break_even

checks.description: Figures that look like a slip, as the page flags them. They don't block the result.

anyOf.description: Days open a week × 52 ÷ 12, one decimal.

figures.description: A month, in the currency of the figures sent.

foodAndDrink.description: Used: opening + purchases - closing with both stock counts, else purchases.

leftOver.description: Left over after every bill at this month's sales, before income tax, to the unit: below 0 when short. Never call it profit.

link.description: Opens the calculator on the website with these figures filled in.

pointValue.description: One point of sales (1%), to the unit: what each point of cost saved leaves a month.

result.description: The result in the page's words, in its order.

scenarios.description: Hourly pay counted one way, or both ways (rising first) when the owner isn't sure and has hourly pay.

anyOf.description: Break-even sales and guests rounded up to the unit, the rest to the nearest unit, as the page shows them. Null: no amount of sales breaks even this way.

cushion.description: Net sales minus break-even: below 0 when short.

cushionPct.description: The cushion, % of net sales, one decimal.

anyOf.description: Sales a month to have the goal left over. Needs goal.
When short, with daysPerWeek and averageSpend: the guests a day that close it.

perThousandOffBills.description: The same, for each 1,000 a month off the bills that stay the same.

pointOffFixed.description: The same, for one point off a fixed bill (salaries).

pointOffRising.description: How far break-even falls a month for one point of sales off a cost that rises with sales.

anyOf.description: When short, with daysPerWeek: the gap a day open.

costsThatRisePct.description: Costs that rise with sales, % of net sales, one decimal. At 100 or more, no amount of sales breaks even.

hourlyPay.description: Counted with the costs that rise with sales, or as a bill that stays the same.

standing.description: The month's net sales against break-even: above it, at it almost exactly, short of it, or never (no amount of sales breaks even, either way).

workedOut.description: How it was worked out, with the figures in each step.

title: Break-even calculator
